name: Security and compliance controls, one provision at a time: NIST SP 800-53, SP 800-171, the SSDF, the Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 and the HIPAA Security Rule in their own words
description: Every control in NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5, every requirement in NIST SP 800-171 Rev 3 (the CMMC baseline), every practice and task in the NIST Secure Software Development Framework (SP 800-218), every category and subcategory of the NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, and every paragraph of the HIPAA Security Rule, cut one provision at a time, each with the publisher's own words as the record's quote. One record is one obligation: a control with five lettered statements becomes five records, keyed the way the publisher cites them (SC-28, SC-28(1), AC-2a, 03.01.01.c.02, PO.1.1, GV.OC-01, 164.312(a)(2)(iv)), so a reader or an agent that has been handed a control number gets that control's text and nothing else. Answers 'what does NIST SP 800-53 SC-28 require', 'what does 800-171 03.05.03 say about multi-factor authentication', 'what does SSDF PW.7.2 require of code review', 'what is CSF 2.0 GV.OC-01', 'what does HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv) actually say about encryption', 'which published controls cover audit logging', and 'what is the organization-defined parameter in AC-12'. The hard part is not finding the documents — NIST publishes all four of its frameworks as machine-readable OSCAL and the eCFR publishes the rule as XML — it is that they are published as whole documents, so a coding assistant asked to implement 'SC-28' or 'PW.7.2' either reads a 1,200-page catalogue or guesses. This dataset is the retrieval layer: provision in, the publisher's sentence out. It does not say how to implement anything, and it never says that any system is compliant; the provision's own text is the whole of what is published here. NIST's machine-readable text leaves a placeholder where a value is the organisation's to decide ('Protect the {{ insert: param, sc-28_odp.01 }} of ...'), so every record that carries one also carries the same sentence with each placeholder resolved from the catalogue's own parameter labels and kept in square brackets — '[Selection (one or more): confidentiality; integrity]' — which is how NIST's own HTML rendering reads, and which is a sentence a person or a coding assistant can actually use. The verbatim text, placeholders and all, stays on the record as the evidence. A provision its publisher has withdrawn is not here at all, whether or not the publisher left its old text in the file. SOC 2, ISO 27001 and PCI DSS are deliberately absent: that text is sold under licence by the bodies that write it and may not be republished, and the licence read of 2026-11-23 found no public mapping of the SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria to fall back on either.
licence: Every source is a US government work in the public domain. NIST publishes SP 800-53, SP 800-171, SP 800-218 and the Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, with their OSCAL renderings in a public GitHub repository, and NIST's own position is that "Works authored by NIST employees are not subject to Copyright protection within the United States"; the Code of Federal Regulations is published by the Office of the Federal Register. NIST asks that its work be cited in its recommended form followed by "Republished courtesy of the National Institute of Standards and Technology", and each record carries that line, links back to the exact file it was cut from and names the publisher's own page for the document. A passage inside a NIST publication that is credited to a third party is outside NIST's grant: the parser reads only the publisher's own provision text and never the `links` blocks where other bodies' clause numbering sits. No text from SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001 or PCI DSS appears anywhere in this dataset, because that text is sold under licence. The whole position, with each publisher's own deciding sentence quoted and the date it was read, is docs/licence-read-2026-11-23-compliance-frameworks.md.

records.framework: HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR part 164, subpart C)
records.requirement: A covered entity or business associate must comply with the applicable standards, implementation specifications, and requirements of this subpart with respect to electronic protected health information of a covered entity.
records.source_quote: A covered entity or business associate must comply with the applicable standards, implementation specifications, and requirements of this subpart with respect to electronic protected health information of a covered entity.

records.source_quote: (a) General requirements. Covered entities and business associates must do the following:

records.requirement: (1) Ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of all electronic protected health information the covered entity or business associate creates, receives, maintains, or transmits.
records.source_quote: (1) Ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of all electronic protected health information the covered entity or business associate creates, receives, maintains, or transmits.

records.requirement: (2) Protect against any reasonably anticipated threats or hazards to the security or integrity of such information.
records.source_quote: (2) Protect against any reasonably anticipated threats or hazards to the security or integrity of such information.

records.requirement: (3) Protect against any reasonably anticipated uses or disclosures of such information that are not permitted or required under subpart E of this part.
records.source_quote: (3) Protect against any reasonably anticipated uses or disclosures of such information that are not permitted or required under subpart E of this part.

records.framework: HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR part 164, subpart C)
records.requirement: (4) Ensure compliance with this subpart by its workforce.
records.source_quote: (4) Ensure compliance with this subpart by its workforce.

records.requirement: (2) In deciding which security measures to use, a covered entity or business associate must take into account the following factors:

records.source_quote: (i) The size, complexity, and capabilities of the covered entity or business associate.

records.framework: HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR part 164, subpart C)
records.requirement: (ii) The covered entity's or the business associate's technical infrastructure, hardware, and software security capabilities.
records.source_quote: (ii) The covered entity's or the business associate's technical infrastructure, hardware, and software security capabilities.

records.framework: HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR part 164, subpart C)
records.requirement: (iii) The costs of security measures.
records.source_quote: (iii) The costs of security measures.

records.framework: HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR part 164, subpart C)
records.requirement: (iv) The probability and criticality of potential risks to electronic protected health information.
records.source_quote: (iv) The probability and criticality of potential risks to electronic protected health information.

records.framework: HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR part 164, subpart C)
records.requirement: (c) Standards. A covered entity or business associate must comply with the applicable standards as provided in this section and in §§ 164.308, 164.310, 164.312, 164.314 and 164.316 with respect to all electronic protected health information.
records.source_quote: (c) Standards. A covered entity or business associate must comply with the applicable standards as provided in this section and in §§ 164.308, 164.310, 164.312, 164.314 and 164.316 with respect to all electronic protected health information.

records.requirement: (d) Implementation specifications. In this subpart:

records.source_quote: (2) When a standard adopted in § 164.308, § 164.310, § 164.312, § 164.314, or § 164.316 includes required implementation specifications, a covered entity or business associate must implement the implementation specifications.

records.framework: NIST SP 800-218 Version 1.1 (Secure Software Development Framework)
records.control_title: Design Software to Meet Security Requirements and Mitigate Security Risks
records.requirement: Identify and evaluate the security requirements for the software; determine what security risks the software is likely to face during operation and how the software’s design and architecture should mitigate those risks; and justify any cases where risk-based analysis indicates that security requirements should be relaxed or waived. Addressing security requirements and risks during software design (secure by design) is key for improving software security and also helps improve development efficiency.
records.source_quote: Identify and evaluate the security requirements for the software; determine what security risks the software is likely to face during operation and how the software’s design and architecture should mitigate those risks; and justify any cases where risk-based analysis indicates that security requirements should be relaxed or waived. Addressing security requirements and risks during software design (secure by design) is key for improving software security and also helps improve development efficiency.
